answer:
AWS rejected the PutBucketPolicy call on rhdp-q8zvw-warehouse with `ExpiredToken`: "The security token included in the request is expired". The credentials were not revoked; they reached the end of their lifetime.

- The job assumes the sandbox role once, at 14:06:53 UTC (`sandbox_aws_session : Assume the sandbox provisioning role`), and every later AWS call uses that session.
- The catalog item `rhpds/agnosticv` `datalake_bu/telemetry-datamart-lab/common.yaml` sets `sandbox_aws_session_duration: 3600`, so the session is valid for one hour.
- The failing call ran at 15:06:58, 60 minutes after the role was assumed. The run (cluster install ~41 minutes plus the datamart workload) is longer than the session, so the session expired mid-run.

The 14:30 key rotation is not the cause. The same session still worked after it: the warehouse bucket was created at 14:54:11. A revoked key would also give InvalidClientTokenId, not ExpiredToken. Re-issuing keys will not change anything.

Fix: raise `sandbox_aws_session_duration` in common.yaml above the run time (for example 10800, which also needs the role's maximum session duration to allow it), or refresh the session before the workload phase.
